translations.answer: Confirm whether the zero in the diagram is the original frame value or the default fill value from the upper computer during frame missing; align TorqueActual with MotorCurrent. Both should not be dropped; continue checking the motor state and feedback frame. This post uses constructed data, and the conclusion must be verified against the original system log.
translations.applicability: Applies to joint platforms that can synchronously collect current, torque, and original bus frames.
translations.credibility.rationale: No reproducible records have been formed.
translations.details.attempts.0: Synchronize torque and current to exclude single torque sensor drift.
translations.details.attempts.1: Check the StatusWord and original frame to distinguish shutdown from frame loss.
translations.details.attempts.2: Suggest adjusting the TPDO period, switching to CAN-FD, splitting the bus, or maintaining/interpolating during frame loss.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Decode torque, current, StatusWord, and temperature using DBC.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Return to the original CAN frame to check for frame loss, do not treat UI fill values as the original bus value.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Check the TPDO period within a time window and by message ID.
translations.details.environments.0: CANopen; demonstration node NodeID=1; target torque 8 N·m; allowable variation ±5%; demonstration period ~40 ms.
translations.details.limits.0: The author explicitly states that DBC, signal data, and timestamps are for demonstration purposes; the tool repository functions are described, but the case result cannot be considered as a real independent repro.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The demonstration case narrows the scope to period frame loss; no real product repair data is provided.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Constant torque command results in zero feedback and joint twitching; how to distinguish sensor, motor, and communication issues?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Do not write zero torque or position without frame loss; use safety-assessed maintenance/interpolation/damping, and set frame loss threshold and emergency stop.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Multiple nodes causing high bus load, TPDO missing in fixed phase period.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The upper computer misinterprets non-received frames as zero.
translations.details.symptoms.0: TorqueActual and MotorCurrent both return to zero and rebound.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The upper computer station experiences periodic twitching.
translations.media_summaries.0: The text table shows 0.020/0.040/0.052 s timing; the author notes it is constructed data, so only process the troubleshooting flow, do not treat the chart as real test evidence.
translations.source.locator: 4.3 section on torque/current timing and zero filling explanation
translations.source.title: Timing Troubleshooting Method for CANopen Joint Torque/Current Oscillation
